name: Elimelech
overview: Elimelech was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the husband of Naomi. His role is noted in the book of Ruth, where his family experiences significant hardship. Beyond his marital relationship, no additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Elimelech means 'G-d is my king,' reflecting a theocentric identity. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a strong declaration of divine sovereignty.
familyAndRelationships: Elimelech was married to Naomi and was the father of Mahlon and Chilion. These relationships are inferred from the scriptural reference in Ruth 1:2, providing a basic family structure important to the narrative.
scriptureSignificance: Elimelech's significance in Scripture lies in his role as the patriarch of a family that faced famine and relocation, setting the stage for the unfolding story of redemption in Ruth. His position as Naomi's husband and father to Mahlon and Chilion connects him to the lineage and providential themes central to the biblical account. Though details about his life are limited, his family circumstances contribute to the broader redemptive history.
